Thanks — reviewed the redlines. High level counsel notes below (see attached PDF for line-by-line tracked comments):

1) Subprocessors / Notice: we should avoid an unconditional 30-day notice requirement. Recommend counter: 30 days for material new subprocessors that process personal data (not for routine infra swaps), and a right for Redwood to use emergency short-notice subprocessors with post-notice confirmation.

2) SCCs vs. EU-US: we can accept that Nimbus prefers SCCs (2021). We'll propose executing SCCs as the transfer mechanism plus an internal annex (export controls + additional safeguards). Legal needs 2-3 business days to prepare the SCC exhibit.

3) Retention carveout: counsel prefers limiting the customer's proposed 3-year carveout to specific transaction records defined by a narrow data category (e.g., billing/transaction logs) and add an automated deletion workflow and retention schedule to Appendix B. This preserves our telemetry/backups by excluding sys-ops telemetry and internal logs.

4) Audit & security assessments: push back on perpetual audit rights. Offer annual SOC/pen-test summaries and on-site audits subject to NDA and scheduling windows.

5) E-sign: no legal objection to DocuSign or AdobeSign. Operationally we default to AdobeSign for enterprise routing. If Nimbus insists on DocuSign, we can provision a one-off DocuSign envelope (legal will need to record the signing flow).

Attachments: RWI_counsel_annotations_round2.pdf, SCCs_2021_comparison.docx

I'll mark the key lines to propose redline language.

- Laura
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection — Redwood Inference

Hi Tom / Elena — thank you for the submission and the clear redlines. We've reviewed internally. Attached is Redwood's annotated response (round 2) with suggested counterlanguage. Summary of our positions: 

- Subprocessor notice: propose compromise language — 30-day notice for material new subprocessors plus emergency exception and monthly subprocessor inventory updates.
- SCCs: happy to execute SCCs (2021). We'll attach our SCC exhibit and a short transfer safeguards annex. Legal expects to finalize within 2 business days.
- Retention carveout: suggest narrowing the scope to 'billing and reconciliation records' only and include an Appendix B retention table that auto-expires other categories.
- Audits: provide SOC 2 report and annual pen test summary; on-site audits available with standard controls (NDA, scheduling, cost allocation).
- E-sign: Redwood prefers AdobeSign for enterprise workflows. We can accommodate DocuSign if Nimbus requires it; please confirm.

Attachments: Redwood_Nimbus_round2_annotated.pdf (line-by-line counters)

Next steps: if you can confirm the e-sign provider and acceptance of SCCs we will prepare the final DPA + SCC exhibit for signature. Also please confirm the delivery address for subprocessor inventory (we will send CSV by June 25).

Best,
Rishi

Rishi — appreciate the fast turnaround and the narrow proposed carveout language. A few quick points from Nimbus legal: 

1) DocuSign preference: Nimbus uses DocuSign as standard. We can accept AdobeSign only if Redwood supplies a short audit trail showing signer identity and certificate-of-signing.
2) Subprocessor cadence: 30-day notice for material subprocessors is acceptable. Please include a definition of 'material' in the DPA (suggested wording: any subprocessor that will process personal data at scale >100k unique records or has access to raw customer content).
3) Retention: the product team insists the 3-year window is important for reconciliation of historical billing disputes. If Redwood can keep the narrow 'billing and reconciliation records' for 3 years, and automatically purge other categories, Nimbus will accept.

We'll review the Redwood_Nimbus_round2_annotated.pdf, but broadly this looks promising. We'll need the SCC exhibit and your subprocessor inventory (CSV) by June 25 to keep the procurement timeline; we have a target signature window of June 28–30.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Senior Privacy Counsel — NimbusRetail
